items.title: China Economics: Back to School, Eyes on September
items.summary: September will be a critical test of whether China's policy push can lead to a cyclical recovery. Meanwhile, we think the window for a rate cut is closing. Instead of budget/bond quota revision, we see actual fund deployment as the key metric to watch for a reversal of de facto austerity.

items.title: Japan Strategy: "Bad" Interest Rate Rises to a Debasement Trade
items.summary: We think the recent sharp decline in Japanese equities stems mainly from rising real interest rates rather than a “debasement trade" linked to deteriorating Japan-U.S. fiscal conditions. During the adjustment phase, defensive value stocks should outperform. We offer more analysis herein.

items.title: China Healthcare: Is AI-Led Drug Discovery the Next Big Thing?
items.summary: AI-driven drug discovery is taking off in China and spurring a lot of investor interest given the speed and cost benefits that AI brings. We see AI wet-lab validation vendors as the most attractive in the near term; longer term, we prefer AI-native drug developers such as Insilico.

items.title: Surging Demand, Strong Execution Drive Strong Beat for Dell
items.summary: Surging demand across key end markets, combined with strong execution, drove a clear beat for Dell. Guidance increased meaningfully with FY27 revenues/EPS growth of ~70%/150% vs. 47%/74% previously. We raise our estimates and lift our target price for Buy-rated DELL to $600 from $515.

items.title: Infineon and STM Are More Than Cyclical Recovery Stories
items.summary: We see more durable earning drivers for Infineon and STMicroelectronics from AI data-center power, automotive content expansion and industrial electrification, with inventory correction largely complete. We prefer Infineon for superior AI power positioning and lower margin execution risk.

items.title: River Disruptions: Buying Opportunity or Value Trap for Viking?
items.summary: Viking faces exceedingly strong demand trends but severe disruptions to its bread-and-butter river cruise business. We unveil a proprietary model of gauge station readings for the key Rhine-Danube river corridor. Despite a tricky near-term setup, we see this as a buying opportunity.

items.title: ADNOC Gas PLC: Oil Flexibility Drives Gas Upside
items.summary: Recent progress in rich gas developments offers further rationale for the UAE’s decision to diverge from OPEC policy. We now see the UAE accounting for 40% of Middle East gas capex this decade, dwarfing its 15% share of production, with ADNOC Gas a clear beneficiary.

items.title: European Tech Hardware & Software: TMT Conference Questions
items.summary: We will host ASML, Capgemini, Infineon, Nokia and STMicroelectronics Sept. 8-10 at our Global TMT Conference in New York. In this note we highlight key themes and share our key questions for the presenting companies.

items.title: North America Transportation: A Global TMT Conference Preview
items.summary: FedEx, CH Robinson and RXO will join us at our Global TMT Conference to discuss how technology is transforming global supply chains and logistics, and how these names are using AI to drive efficiency. We hope to delve deeper into topics often overlooked by traditional transports investors.

items.title: What Works in Equity Markets: Residualized Momentum
items.summary: Price Momentum strategies are often susceptible to momentum crashes that typically occur during market turning points, macroeconomic regime shifts, or rapid style rotations. We explore how to address some of these vulnerabilities using "Residualized Momentum," with more details herein.

items.title: Asia Pacific Radar Screen: The Value-Momentum Seesaw
items.summary: MSCI Asia Pacific ex Japan recovered 3% in August, bringing yet another reversal in Value vs. Momentum. Relative Value was down 6.6% as Composite Momentum gained 5.4%, giving us an almost flat Radar. Currently the model favors Korea, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Global Commodities: Weather Risks Intensify Across Softs
items.summary: Weather risks are becoming increasingly important across the ICE softs complex, but market outcomes remain highly differentiated by inventory levels and balance-sheet dynamics. For sugar, a host of factors reinforce our bullish view; it's where we continue to see the greatest upside risk.

items.title: U.S. Rates Strategy: Hyperscaler Supply and the UST Curve
items.summary: The curve is flattening following Treasury’s larger buyback announcement. But will hyperscaler issuance continue to put upward pressure on the long end? We see risks specifically at the 30y point, but note the Fed and Treasury should remain the main influences for the remainder of 2026.

items.title: Middle East Economics: The Conflict’s Uneven Macroeconomic Impact
items.summary: Six months into the U.S.-Iran conflict, economic performance across the Gulf economies has differed markedly. We examine where the shock has landed across production, activity, prices and credit and note that the outlook depends heavily on how long the disruption will persist.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Second-Half Playbook
items.summary: We see Software's recent rebound as driven mainly by positioning and narrative and not fundamentals. Looking to the second half, our stock selection favors AI infrastructure-layer fundamental acceleration plays and names with M&A/takeout optionality. We review our top picks in this note.

items.title: European Credit Insights: AI Debt Layers — A European Perspective
items.summary: The AI infrastructure buildout is being financed through an increasingly complex stack of hyperscaler bonds, data-center project finance, neo-cloud funding and GPU-backed vehicles. We map the different layers of leverage against the revenue commitments underwriting the buildout.

items.title: North America Hardware & Storage: HDD Megatrends
items.summary: We highlight key takeaways from a call with storage experts TrendFocus. The HDD industry continues to benefit from the combination of powerful secular demand growth and constrained supply, with AI accelerating data creation and expanding long-term storage requirements.

items.title: Spain Banks: Second-Quarter Market-Share Heatmap
items.summary: We update Spanish banks’ market-share trends for the second quarter. We see BBVA as the standout performer, gaining market share year over year in both loans and deposits. CABK and SAN also showed strong commercial momentum in loans and market share. We offer more takeaways herein.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Data > Warsh
items.summary: Chair Warsh was unambiguously hawkish at Jackson Hole, but we see data remaining a primary policy driver, with further softening ahead of the next FOMC meeting. That should weigh on the USD as the market removes hawkish pricing. The more bullish USD factor remains the Middle East conflict.

items.title: We're Downgrading Daikin Industries to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading Daikin Industries to Neutral, as its attempts to improve profitability and narrow the OPM gap with U.S. peers look increasingly unlikely to succeed. Our sense is that investors are increasingly frustrated by the slow pace of change. We lower our target price to ¥22,500.

items.title: 2026 Global TMT Conference Preview: Key Tech Themes to Watch
items.summary: Our Global TMT Conference, held Sept. 8-10 in New York, will test market debates and explore thematic pillars, spanning AI infrastructure, enterprise AI diffusion, physical AI, and more. We offer 10 key themes to watch in this note, highlighting opportunities, risks, and actionable ideas.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: The Intelligence Flywheel
items.summary: Open-weight models have reached 53% of Vercel AI Gateway token volume, up 24 points from late June, with the frontier proprietary vs. frontier open-weight intelligence gap narrowing to 3 points from 9. We look at how open-weight models can support attractive economics in this note.

items.title: Mexico's Market Performance Has Repriced Uncertainty
items.summary: Mexico's economic activity rebounded in the second quarter, but momentum weakened as the quarter advanced. We continue to see the impact of El Niño as considerably less severe than in other Latin American economies. We explore what we think is behind equity-market weakness in this note.

items.title: Canada Economics Weekly: New Tariffs, New Dovish Risk
items.summary: Canada's trade talks with the U.S. fell apart and new tariffs went into effect. Given new headwinds for demand, we expect the recent escalation of trade tensions to have net dovish implications for policymakers and continue to see 50 basis points in additional rate cuts ahead.

items.title: Second Quarter Was Strong for China Banks
items.summary: 21 covered China banks posted stronger-than-expected pre-provision operating profit growth of 10.2% year over year in the second quarter, lifted by strong trading gains, resilient loan growth and stabilizing net interest margin. We review which names delivered beats and which disappointed.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Softer Data Vs. a September Hike
items.summary: Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was more hawkish than expected, leading markets to again price more than a 50% chance of a September hike. Despite Warsh downplaying recent data, we don't think he explicitly indicated a policy move, and think soft-enough data will keep rates unchanged.

items.title: U.S. Equity Strategy: Broadening Trade Nuance
items.summary: The broadening trade discussion remains topical with investors. In this note, we provide a quick side-by-side comparison of S&P 500 Equal Weight vs SMID. Generally, SMID provides more economic sensitivity whereas Equal Weight tends to have more defensive characteristics.

items.title: Off the Cuff: Jackson Hole Perspective and Implications
items.summary: Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech reemphasized commitment to a 2% inflation target. Other commentary pointed to stable economic data, but with some mention that financial conditions aren't restrictive and may be on the easier side. We offer further takeaways from the speech in this note.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Shuffling the AI Deck
items.summary: The AI trade has seen trading fits and starts, with the longer-term set up and implications still a bit opaque — consistent with our view that the Mag 7 is less relevant as a tradeable cohort. Still, we need both the AI-affected and broadening tailwinds to reach our 8100 S&P 500 target.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: UST Concerns Amid the Global Bond Glut
items.summary: Bessent may get what he wants. Our Global Bond Glut framework sees excess supply as well-priced, with yields having co-moved higher mainly with energy and slightly with equities -- this is an Iran and growth problem. We look at the good and bad news for Bessent, and how to bridge the gap.

items.title: Global FX: Signs of a Bessent Doctrine?
items.summary: The intervention under the “currency alliance” between the U.S. and Japan could be seen as sign of change in global policy, though we believe efforts to rectify global imbalances led by Bessent are likely to adopt an approach completely different from that of 1985's Plaza Accord.

items.title: Macro-to-Micro: Decoding India's Credit Surge
items.summary: India may be in its second credit surge, with the credit-to-GDP ratio breaking past the last 15 years’ range. We analyze the broader credit trends beyond banking and delve into sectoral decomposition. We focus on rising household debt to understand whether it requires policy intervention.

items.title: European Auto Manufacturers: Is Risk-Reward Finally Improving?
items.summary: The third quarter looks like a tough one for European auto makers, but we believe there's room for a relief rally in the sector from these low levels. Tactically, we think the risk-reward for any such move is most positive with Porsche, BMW and Forvia. We offer further details herein.

items.title: Is the Return to Venezuela About to Accelerate?
items.summary: The U.S. and Venezuela are reportedly discussing the U.S. taking stakes in a number of oilfields, to be developed by private firms. We think this opportunity reflects a broader theme, explored in this note: The next round of material oil volume growth will likely come outside of the U.S.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Food Inflation Poses Risks
items.summary: Markets are increasingly discounting geopolitical risks amid slower-than-expected oil inventory drawdowns, but we see food inflation as the bigger medium-term risk. As we explore in this note, such upside inflation risks could constrain dovish emerging-markets central-bank pricing.

items.title: NVIDIA's Revenue Outlook Tops Expectations
items.summary: NVIDIA reported better-than-expected results and said its FY28 revenue outlook is for 70% year-over-year growth lifted by agentic AI demand, though gross margin outlook is being reset slightly lower. We raise our FY27-29 EPS for Buy-rated NVDA and lift our target price to $315.

items.title: Meta Settlement Removes an Overhang for Shares
items.summary: We believe Meta's $18 billion settlement around teen usage removes a significant overhang in shares and comes at a time when its AI product roadmap is emerging. While terms of the settlement pose some risk to engagement, we see the operational impact as likely to be somewhat limited.

items.title: Deep Dive: Why Axa's Time Could Be Now
items.summary: We examine Axa’s delivery over its 2023-26 plan and preview its 2026-29 plan, expected next month. We see the new plan delivering a 9% CAGR through 2029, given a transformational productivity opportunity and multiple levers for positive EPS surprises, and open a positive Catalyst Watch.

items.title: We See Oracle's Historic Selloff As an Opportunity
items.summary: We're opening a positive catalyst watch on Oracle and raise our FY28-30 revenue EPS well above consensus and targets. We see opportunity after one of the most extreme dislocations and drawdowns in the stock's history, driven by investor capitulation and multiple technical selling factors.

items.title: UPS Investors Are Being Well-Compensated for Risks
items.summary: UPS described a generally constructive operating environment, with cost-cutting and efficiency efforts starting to be reflected in margin stabilization. We think its depressed valuation more than compensates for uncertainties driving investor skepticism, offering a compelling risk-reward.

items.title: South Korea Raises Rates, But Hurdles Look High for October Hike
items.summary: South Korea raised rates 25 basis points, with Governor Shin rationalizing the back-to-back hikes by noting the importance of preemptive action and early response. But the hurdles look high for an October hike, leaving us continuing to expect 25-bps hikes in November and February.

items.title: We Now Expect Australia to Raise Rates in September
items.summary: Given Australia's latest household-spending data, we now expect a 25-basis-point rate hike in September instead of November. But institutionally dovish policymakers may push back, and we think it's likely that dissenters will increase in September. We explore potential paths herein.
